fish.name: Salt Wisp
fish.flavor: Barely a fish; mostly a rumor with fins. It dissolves into sea spray if you stop looking at it, so don't.

fish.name: Buttonfish
fish.flavor: Round, shiny, and exactly the size of a coat button. Sailors sew them onto oilskins for luck; the fish have not consented to this.

fish.name: Grey Yawner
fish.flavor: It yawns constantly, which would be rude if anything out here cared. Watching one too long is the leading cause of naps at sea.

fish.name: Penny Skipper
fish.flavor: Skips across the swells like a flat stone thrown by someone very patient. Worth about a penny; sentimentally priceless.

fish.name: Fog Herring
fish.flavor: It only schools in fog, or possibly it is the fog. Either way, your lantern is useless, and it thinks that's funny.

fish.name: Knot Eel
fish.flavor: Ties itself into a granny knot whenever it gets nervous, which is always. Untying one before release is considered good manners.

fish.name: Bilge Smelt
fish.flavor: Smells like the inside of a boot and the bottom of a boat. Loved by absolutely no one, caught by absolutely everyone.

fish.name: Wobbletail
fish.flavor: Swims like it is still deciding whether to. Naturalists have confirmed the wobble is load-bearing.

fish.name: Lantern Sprat
fish.flavor: A pocket-sized glow that follows boats home in the dark. Old sailors say it's rude to catch the one lighting your way. Old sailors say a lot of things.

fish.name: Bootlace Blenny
fish.flavor: Long, thin, and always coming undone. In a pinch it will keep an entire crew's boots tied, provided nobody mentions it.

fish.name: Murmur Cod
fish.flavor: It murmurs, low and constant, just below hearing. Nobody has made out the words yet, but the tone is unmistakably gossip.

fish.name: Swellhopper
fish.flavor: Rides the biggest waves all the way up and never quite comes down the same fish. Ask it about the view. It won't stop anyway.

fish.name: Drizzlefin
fish.flavor: Wherever it surfaces, a light rain follows within the hour. Meteorologists despise it. Gardeners row out specially to find it.

fish.name: Whistling Pilchard
fish.flavor: Whistles a sea shanty that has no ending. Entire crews have gone hoarse trying to finish the chorus for it.

fish.name: Cradle Sole
fish.flavor: Flat and soft as a well-worn pillow. Folklore says one kept under the bunk grants dreamless sleep; folklore does not mention the smell.

fish.name: Humdrum Haddock
fish.flavor: A perfectly ordinary haddock, which out here, among all this strangeness, is the strangest thing of all. It refuses to elaborate.

fish.name: Left-Handed Halibut
fish.flavor: Both eyes migrated the wrong way and it has been swimming apologetically ever since. Left-handed sailors swear it brings luck; everyone else swears it's just lost.

fish.name: Moonspit Mackerel
fish.flavor: Silver as a coin and twice as slippery. Fisherfolk say they're flecks of moonlight the sea swallowed and politely returned.

fish.name: Sighing Gurnard
fish.flavor: Produces one long, theatrical sigh when landed, then stares at the horizon. It's fine. It says it's fine. Do not worry about it.

fish.name: Backwards Barracuda
fish.flavor: Swims tail-first at alarming speed. Nobody knows where it's going, but it has an excellent view of where it's been.

fish.name: Knitting Needlefish
fish.flavor: They work in pairs, weaving kelp into tiny scarves that nobody wears. The craftsmanship, frankly, is excellent.

fish.name: Umbrella Ray
fish.flavor: Opens itself flat over smaller fish whenever it rains. Rain, underwater? Ask the Drizzlefin. The ray is just being considerate.

fish.name: The Polite Angler
fish.flavor: Its lure glows a soft, welcoming amber, and it always lets its prey finish their sentence first. Standards matter, even down here.

fish.name: Gossip Grouper
fish.flavor: Loiters under hulls, listening. Whatever you said about the first mate last Tuesday, it knows, and it has already told the gulls.

fish.name: Salt Choir Sardine
fish.flavor: Never caught alone. Each one hums a single sustained note, and a full school has been known to perform entire funerals for passing ships.

fish.name: Fiddler's Conger
fish.flavor: Its long body thrums like a bowed string in strong current. On calm nights, the whole ocean is its instrument, and it only knows sad songs.

fish.name: The Ferryman's Change
fish.flavor: Its scales are worn silver coins, every one from a different sunken purse. It circles old wrecks patiently, making change for the crossing.

fish.name: Weathercock Wrasse
fish.flavor: Always faces tomorrow's wind. Captains who follow its nose come home. Captains who don't come home eventually.

fish.name: Ninth Wave
fish.flavor: Folklore says it is born inside the ninth wave of every ninth swell. It arrives precisely when the sea decides you have earned it, and not one wave sooner.

fish.name: The Bellringer
fish.flavor: It strikes the bells of sunken wrecks with its armored brow, keeping perfect time for a port that drowned before clocks were invented.

fish.name: Foglantern
fish.flavor: A cold green light drifting where no boat should be. Follow it once and you'll find fish. Follow it twice and it will find you.

fish.name: Sea-Wife's Mirror
fish.flavor: So perfectly silvered you can check your reflection in its side. The reflection runs a few seconds slow, and lately it has started waving first.

fish.name: Widdershins Shark
fish.flavor: Circles boats counterclockwise only, quietly undoing small curses as it goes. A shark circling the other way is just a shark. Be careful out there.

fish.name: Grandmother Teeth
fish.flavor: An old, old shark with a mouth of mismatched teeth, folklore says one from every fish that ever bit her. She is very gentle now. Mostly.

fish.name: The Cartographer's Folly
fish.flavor: The markings on its back form a flawless map of a coastline that does not exist. Three expeditions have set out anyway. Two came back different.

fish.name: Vesper Maw
fish.flavor: It rises at evening bell with its great mouth open, swallowing the day's last light so the dark can come in on schedule. It does seem sorry about it.

fish.name: The Second Moon
fish.flavor: A pale, round enormity that surfaces only on moonless nights, so the tide never has to feel alone. Astronomers have declined to comment.

fish.name: The Drowned Bell
fish.flavor: Not a bell, but a fish that grieves like one. Its toll rolls along the keel and up through your boots, and every sailor aboard suddenly remembers a door they left open.

fish.name: Mother of Storms
fish.flavor: The old charts write her name inside every inked storm cloud. When she breaches, the horizon flinches, and for one held breath the rain falls upward.

fish.name: Grandfather Undertow
fish.flavor: Every current is a finger of his hand, and every lost thing sleeps somewhere in his beard. He takes your bait out of politeness, and lets you land him because you looked like you needed it.
